nodes.body: A better solution for naming these may just be to make the arguments proper `enum`s.
To be clear, I don't consider this to be a blocker. It would make a good follow-up, however.

Agree, enum is cleaner. Since it is not blocker, and the scope of the changes to do clean changes are big (see below), how about let's do it at subsequent PR? I filed issue #4732 to track it.

More details:
the two parameters are declared as `bool aligned, bool dma` in main's `view.hpp`, `views.hpp` and `expr.hpp`. An `enum class` value does not convert to `bool`. So the enum change must edit those three headers, plus `slice.hpp`, `tensor.hpp`, `dotter.hpp` and the five `static constexpr bool dma` members. It must also rewrite the 80 existing call sites (82 lines in 20 files) that pass bare `true, false`. 

Your #4697 keeps `bool Dma` in its new aliases. So the enum change should land after #4697. I am taking #4697 into this branch first.

Can we rename this to say VNNI:


```suggestion
// Note [VNNI Packed V layout]
```
It is updated at latest commit.
I'm not sure I understand what Claude is trying to say here. Can you clarify?

Alright, reading again I think I am beginning to see. It looks like Claude is (rightly) playing language lawyer. The C++ spec states that an implicitly-created object's  (that is, one not introduced by a `new` expression) lifetime must begin in an `operator new`. Consequently, the previous implementation was strictly-speaking incorrect: it allocated storage but failed to actually begin the lifetime of the object residing in that storage.

Previously this was perhaps okay since the storage held POD, but now it contains a `v_vnni_tensor`, requiring that we be a bit more careful.

I think it would be good to reword the Note more clearly.
Sorry I did not ease the pain enough, it took me quite an effort understanding it. The comments are updated, please let me know if it is accurate.
Oof, this seems unfortunate. We should open a ticket to fix this. Leaving the bounds of the specified language is fraught with peril, especially in a language filled with as many sharp edges as C++
I filed issue #4588 and planned to address it after this PR. Thanks for resolving it at PR #4698.

This is a rather subtle pattern that is repeated quite a few times. I have opened #4697 to deduplicate this. Feel free to merge or adapt to taste.
Thanks, I merged #4697.

This row makes "a float NaN stores as +inf" a tested contract. AGENTS.md treats NaN as corruption; this pins the path that hides it. The truncation and tie rows likewise pin today's rounding, with no named consumer. Suggest dropping the NaN->inf and rounding rows and keeping the bf16 bit-exact round trip and partner-zero checks.

This is the only check of the packed layout against an independent formula, but it sits after the `available()` early return (line 197), so it silently skips on hosts without AMX. The `at()` section in t_llama_unit doesn't cover it: `at()` and `append_v_row` share `pair_base`, so a wrong formula passes both. Move it above the early return, or into t_llama_unit.

`native_k_view` is an alias of the generic row-major `view`, and t_llama_unit asserts it is constructible from `const bf16*`. So any pointer or row-major 64x128 bf16 view passes the QK kernel; "a bare pointer is a compile error" holds for V only. Fine as a first step, but please say so in the description and give K a distinct type in #4424.

As this line says, nothing can catch a regression here, and it adds a global `operator new[]` overload in a widely included header. It's a correct reading of [intro.object], but since it came from 39a68994465f3fb753623eec18378544be806862 rather than #4698, it'd be good to get @bgamari-positron's explicit sign-off on the approach.

[39a6899 ](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/commit/39a68994465f3fb753623eec18378544be806862) is [responding to Ben's request](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/4557#discussion_r4159939672) of updating the comment.

The kernel probes above (bare pointer / other plane's view rejected) are the PR's real contract. Several of these only document structure (test policy): no `operator[]`, no view of a temporary, not default-constructible, `sizeof`/`alignof`. And the three trivial-type checks repeat `static_assert`s that kv_cache.hpp already makes. Suggest keeping the kernel probes and dropping the rest.

This `GENERATE` and the new "token copies keep bits in all four parity combinations" section (line 3664) both run all four `copy_token` parities through `book::append`; the bit-exact one covers more. One parity here already protects the NaN zeroing, so one of these is duplicate coverage.
Nit: the section is still named "append_v preserves poison", but it now asserts that the poison is zeroed.
